correctness.rationale: Any feasible selection requires at least two vertices on each side. For a selected a_i the number of unselected neighbors is n-1-y+1_{i in J}; analogous expression holds for b_j. Thus capacity and domination give precisely the two classified overlap regimes, and binomial index-subset counts yield the polynomial. Minimization gives 4 at r=1; 2r for n>=2r and 2r+2 otherwise, with the displayed equality cases. Fresh independent adjacency-mask brute force tested 101,952 subsets for n=3..7 across all allowable k and checked every coefficient.
